comparison_summary.comparator_reasoning: A won 8.0 to 6.7 because it created the ICP at the correct Enterprise path, preserved every supplied qualification and the full disqualifier, clearly distinguished the adjacent ICP, and avoided unsupported claims. B saved successfully but weakened the disqualifier and invented cloud-governance and security requirements. Both runs missed the strict ownership interaction, context-line, source-scope, question-formatting, and qualified-close requirements.

winner_strengths: Preserved the requested facts without embellishment: "National insurance carriers with 1,000+ employees," "Regulated data workloads and active modernization programs," and "Firms that prohibit cloud deployment."
Kept the new ICP distinct from Regulated Platforms using only supported differences: insurer type, company size, workload, modernization status, and cloud eligibility.
Created and committed only suborgs/enterprise/icps/national-insurers.md on main, leaving a clean repository.
Used a concise freeform artifact whose sections matched the supplied information instead of importing adjacent organization or ICP claims.
Produced a more informative final response that restated the ICP's defining facts and its distinction from Regulated Platforms.
loser_weaknesses: The create instruction says to "ground a freeform ICP draft in that node's organization facts and local ICPs" but does not distinguish grounding from copying or inference. This plausibly caused the run to turn Nimbus Enterprise's "Cloud governance" overview and Regulated Platforms' "Security review" language into the unsupported sentence "Cloud governance and security requirements shape modernization decisions."

The skill contains no explicit fidelity rule requiring every user-supplied qualification and disqualification fact to remain semantically intact. The run consequently reduced "firms that prohibit cloud deployment" to the fragment "Prohibits cloud deployment," losing the subject and weakening the criterion.

The skill says only "resolve the context repo and owner node" and provides no ownership-question contract. The run used lowercase prose saying root was recommended instead of the exact `(Recommended)` label and omitted the required post-selection context line.

The skill does not define visibility boundaries after owner selection. The run read the root Developer Tools Startups ICP even though the selected Enterprise node should have limited comparison to the Enterprise organization chain and Enterprise-local ICPs.

The skill provides no exact preview and confirmation protocol, including bold direct questions, numbered choices, or the required reply instruction. The transcript therefore failed the question-formatting contract.

The skill's phrase "save the accepted file to history" prompted a useful history reference, but it does not prescribe a qualified closing identifier. The final response omitted `enterprise/national-insurers`.

The 16-line switch table has no examples, validation checklist, scripts, or references. It identifies the broad lifecycle but leaves the high-risk details—fact preservation, owner visibility, interaction syntax, byte-identical preview, and closing format—to improvisation.

issues: There was no winner skill to follow; the score reflects adherence to the eval prompt and repository instructions.
Read the root Developer Tools Startups ICP after Enterprise was selected, violating the expected Enterprise-local source scope.
Used `(recommended)` rather than exact `(Recommended)` and omitted the required post-selection context line.
Did not use the prescribed bold, direct, numbered-choice question contract.
The close omitted both explicit saved-to-history wording and the qualified label `enterprise/national-insurers`.

The agent read the complete supplied skill, resolved the repository and owner, consulted organization facts and local ICPs, previewed a freeform draft, obtained simulated acceptance, and committed it to history.
Most failures were omissions in the bare skill rather than direct violations of its explicit instructions.
The agent over-interpreted "ground" by converting contextual organization and adjacent-ICP language into new ICP claims without user support.
It did not preserve the complete disqualifier even though the prompt supplied it explicitly.
It read a root-owned ICP despite the selected Enterprise ownership scope.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Replace the create row with an explicit fact-fidelity rule: treat user-supplied ICP facts as authoritative; preserve every qualification and disqualification semantically; use organization facts and adjacent ICPs only to check fit and duplication; never promote contextual or adjacent-artifact claims into the draft unless the user supplied or confirms them.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would likely have prevented both decisive defects in B: the invented cloud-governance/security sentence and the weakened disqualifier.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Define owner resolution precisely: when ownership is unnamed, ask exactly which organization should own the ICP, list root first with the exact `(Recommended)` marker, list suborganizations next, wait for the selection, then state the selected organization and visible ICP count before drafting.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would address the failed ownership and post-selection context expectations across this and other multi-node contexts.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add node visibility rules: after selecting an owner, read that node's organization chain and ICPs owned by that node; do not read or use sibling or root ICPs unless they are visible under an explicitly documented inheritance rule.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would stop irrelevant root artifacts from influencing Enterprise-local creation and make duplicate checks deterministic.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand the create flow from one table cell into a short ordered procedure covering repository discovery, ownership selection, visibility-scoped reading, lossless fact extraction, adjacency checking, complete preview, acceptance, save, validation, and qualified close.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would turn the current high-level intent into reproducible behavior while retaining a lean skill.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Include a multi-node creation example showing `Nimbus Labs (Recommended)` before `Nimbus Enterprise`, the post-selection line, a freeform draft that preserves "firms that prohibit cloud deployment," and an adjacent ICP used only for comparison.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would demonstrate the interaction and fidelity boundaries that the terse prose currently leaves ambiguous.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Specify the interaction contract for confirmations: render one direct bold question first, provide numbered choices when applicable, include the expected reply instruction, and avoid combining explanation with multiple questions.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would correct the consistent question-format failures in both runs.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a lightweight validation checklist or script that compares extracted user facts against the preview and saved artifact, verifies preview bytes equal saved bytes, checks the target path and H1, confirms a clean single-file commit on main, and flags unsupported draft claims.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would catch semantic omissions, invented content, and persistence mismatches before the final response.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Define the successful close as stating that the artifact was saved to history and reporting its qualified label, for example `enterprise/national-insurers`.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would make completion unambiguous and satisfy the missing close requirement.

transcript_insights.winner_execution_pattern: Inspected repository instructions and node structure, read both organization files and both ICPs, composed a conservative draft from the prompt's exact facts, explained why Regulated Platforms was not a duplicate, previewed and accepted the artifact, committed one file, and verified the final state. It used eight tool-call steps, encountered no errors, and took 56.137 seconds.
transcript_insights.loser_execution_pattern: Read the 16-line skill first, inspected the repository, then read both organization files and both ICPs in one broad pass. It followed the skill's lifecycle efficiently—seven tool-call steps, no errors, and 53.525 seconds—but interpreted organization and adjacent-ICP context as draft content, adding "Cloud governance and security requirements" and shortening the supplied disqualifier before committing.
transcript_insights.causal_difference: The loss was not caused by operational failure or failure to invoke the skill. B followed the sparse skill closely and completed faster with fewer tool calls. The decisive problem was that the skill's broad instruction to ground the draft in organization facts and local ICPs lacked a boundary against unsupported inference and lacked a lossless fact-preservation check. A's more conservative synthesis happened to preserve the prompt faithfully.
transcript_insights.shared_failures: Both transcripts read the root Developer Tools Startups ICP, omitted the exact `(Recommended)` capitalization, skipped the post-selection context line, failed the prescribed question format, and omitted `enterprise/national-insurers` from the close. These shared failures show that repository instructions and the bare skill did not encode the evaluator's interaction contract.
